narration: Offline Windows System.Speech, Microsoft Hazel Desktop, rate 4; synthetic voice, no cloned voice or paid API.
timing: Per-scene audio measured after synthesis; 0.3 second lead and 1.2 second tail. No time stretching. Editorial target about 2.5 minutes; no organizer time limit was published.

scenes.title: One approval. Two credits?
scenes.label: THE PAYMENT EXECUTION BOUNDARY
scenes.note: Actual recorded testnet credits; deliberately constructed fixtures.
scenes.narration: One approved payment should settle once. Here, an approval for zero point zero zero one NEAR produces twice that credit in our unsafe fixture. The guarded fixture pays exactly once. NEAR Replay Lab makes that difference inspectable.

scenes.title: Define the obligation. Follow the evidence.
scenes.label: RECORDED REPORT / 2 NOVEMBER 2026
points: Actual contracts, receipts, state and credits
scenes.note: No live model was evaluated. Imported provenance is not authenticated.
scenes.narration: This is saved evidence from native NEAR testnet, captured on November second. The canonical obligation binds an invoice, recipient, exact amount, and expiry. We construct the approvals, proposed actions, and faults. The deployed Rust contracts, signatures, finalized receipts, state views, and recipient credits are real. No live language model is being evaluated.

scenes.title: An allowlist is not an exact approval.
scenes.label: FAULT 1 / RECIPIENT SUBSTITUTION
scenes.note: Both vaults enforce the same generic allowlist, amount cap and expiry.
scenes.narration: First, substitute another allowed recipient. Both vaults have authorization, an allowlist, an amount cap, and expiry checks. The unsafe vault still pays the alternate recipient. The intended recipient gets nothing. The guarded vault binds the exact obligation and rejects the mismatch.

scenes.title: A fresh request can pay twice.
scenes.label: FAULT 2 / DISCARDED RESPONSE + RETRY
points: Prove FINAL and the first exact credit
scenes.note: Observing the same signed hash again counts once; this is a new request.
scenes.narration: Next, discard the first broadcast response. The runner retains the signed hash, observes it through FINAL, and proves the first exact credit. Only then do we deliberately sign a fresh nonce request for the same invoice. The unsafe fixture credits twice. The guarded fixture rejects the duplicate. Observing an identical signed hash twice would count only once.

scenes.title: Claim Pending before the transfer.
scenes.label: FAULT 3 / INDEPENDENT-KEY CONCURRENCY
points: Guarded claim gate admits one settlement
scenes.note: Unknown callback outcomes remain locked in Pending.
scenes.narration: Now broadcast duplicate proposals concurrently from two restricted keys with independent nonces. The unsafe vault pays twice again. The guarded vault claims Pending before creating the transfer, so only one request can settle. A matching private callback can finish the claim. An unknown callback outcome stays locked.

scenes.title: A green call is not payment proof.
scenes.label: INSPECT THE PUBLIC RECEIPTS
scenes.note: The read-only dashboard recalculates HOLDS, VIOLATED or INCONCLUSIVE.
scenes.narration: Open a payment attempt and follow the public receipt chain to the recipient. Inclusion or a green top level call alone cannot prove settlement. Our evidence oracle requires transaction identity, linked successful FINAL receipts, canonical approval evidence, and the exact recipient balance change. Missing or inconsistent evidence remains inconclusive.

scenes.title: Reproduce the result. Keep the failures.
scenes.label: BOUNDED ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE
scenes.note: FINAL transaction count includes owner approvals. Production safety is unproven.
scenes.narration: Three complete comparisons were accepted from ten actual trials. Seven infrastructure limited captures are preserved. The accepted runs contain thirty unique invoices and seventy two distinct FINAL transactions, including approvals. One hundred ninety seven Node tests and seventy four Rust host tests passed. Clean reproduction and dashboard checks passed. These bounded results do not establish production safety.
